name: vnc-desktop-view
description: See and control your remote Windows, Linux or Mac desktop, with sound and clipboard, in an editor tab over your existing Remote Tunnels / Remote-SSH connection
author: Rob Derr <robjderr@gmail.com>

enumDescriptions: Text copied on the remote lands on your clipboard; your clipboard is sent when you paste in the desktop tab.
Only send your clipboard to the remote (when you paste there); the remote never changes your clipboard.
Only take text copied on the remote; your clipboard is never sent.
vncDesktopView.clipboard.markdownDescription: Clipboard sync with the remote desktop. Your clipboard is only sent when you paste (Ctrl+V / ⌘V) in the desktop tab. Choose `toRemote` if programs on the remote shouldn't be able to change your clipboard, `off` for no sync at all.

enumDescriptions: ⌘ acts as Ctrl on the remote, so ⌘C, ⌘V, ⌘Z… work like on the Mac.
⌘ is sent as the Windows key.
vncDesktopView.commandKey.markdownDescription: Mac only: what the ⌘ (Command) key sends to the remote desktop.

enumDescriptions: Ask the first time a Linux remote has no usable hardware encoder.
Use OpenH264 when there is no usable hardware encoder (downloaded from Cisco when first needed).
Always use OpenH264, even when there is a hardware encoder (for comparison, or if the GPU encoder misbehaves). Downloaded from Cisco when first needed.
vncDesktopView.openH264.markdownDescription:
Linux remotes without a usable hardware H.264 encoder: use the **OpenH264** software encoder instead, downloaded once from Cisco to the remote machine. It uses more CPU than a GPU encoder.

*OpenH264 Video Codec provided by Cisco Systems, Inc.*
